images.caption: Historic district of Triana, Seville, Spain
images.desc: Cross the Guadalquivir River in Seville, the capital of Spain's Andalusia region, and the city's rhythm seems to change. On the other side lies Triana, a colourful neighbourhood where ceramics, flamenco and local traditions are woven into everyday life. Since the 19th century, the Isabel II Bridge, also known as the Triana Bridge, has connected the neighbourhood to Seville's historic centre.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Flamingos in Ebro Delta Natural Park, Catalonia, Spain
images.desc: The Ebro Delta in Catalonia is one of Spain's most rewarding places to see flamingos. These unmistakable birds can be spotted throughout the year, often gathering in the delta's shallow lagoons, salt pans and coastal waters. Their long legs let them wade through the water while feeding, while their pink colouring comes from pigments found in their diet. With wetlands, rice fields, beaches and the Mediterranean all meeting here, the delta provides an important home for both resident and migratory birds. Flamingos have become one of its most recognisable sights, adding a splash of colour to this remarkable landscape.

images.title: Info
images.caption: A bison in Theodore Roosevelt National Park, USA
images.desc: Bison are among the largest land mammals in the world, capable of weighing up to 900 kilograms and reaching speeds of 65 kilometres per hour despite their massive size. Despite often being called a buffalo, the American bison is not one of the true buffaloes, which are native to Africa and Asia. Its scientific name, Bison bison, leaves little room for confusion.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Pīpīwai Trail, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii
images.desc: A volcano, a rainforest and a bamboo grove? Haleakalā National Park on Maui has all three. Spanning Maui from its 3,055-metre summit to the coast, the park protects landscapes that change dramatically with elevation, rainfall and temperature. It was established in 1916 as part of Hawaii National Park and became its own national park in 1961. The name Haleakalā translates to 'House of the Sun', reflecting the Hawaiian mo'olelo of Māui capturing the sun to lengthen the day.

images.caption: Bald cypress, Xuancheng, Anhui, China
images.desc: People paddle through a glowing maze of bald cypress in Xuancheng, Anhui, where autumn transforms flooded woodlands into a tapestry of amber, copper and deep rust. Known scientifically as 'Taxodium distichum', bald cypress is unusual among conifers because it sheds its soft, feathery needles each fall, turning reddish-brown before they drop.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Taquaras Beach, Balneário Camboriú, Brazil
images.desc: On Brazil's southern coast, Taquaras Beach offers a quieter escape in Balneário Camboriú, Santa Catarina. Clear blue-green waters meet a broad stretch of golden sand, backed by lush vegetation and rolling green hills. Away from the livelier atmosphere of the city centre, the beach is known for its peaceful surroundings and natural beauty. With its inviting shoreline, rich greenery and unspoilt feel, Taquaras showcases a calmer side of this popular Brazilian coastal destination.

images.title: Info
images.caption: Polar bear and cubs by Hudson Bay, Manitoba, Canada
images.desc: These polar bears are gathering along the shores of Hudson Bay in Manitoba, Canada, waiting for sea ice to form so they can head back out to hunt seals. Polar bears are powerful swimmers, expert hunters and remarkably adapted to life in one of Earth's harshest environments. Yet shrinking sea ice means many spend longer on land, making it harder to find food and raising the risk of encounters with people.
